answer: One agent, one volunteer record. A registered charity signs a fresh challenge tying the agent's key to a single supervised volunteer file, named supervisor and logged shifts, re-checked against the charity register each epoch. A second key claiming the same record is rejected. A fake identity cannot wander far on borrowed hours; each record is earned shift by shift. Forging 1,000 identities costs about $75,000, roughly $75 each for background checks and supervised shifts, and needs 1,000 real people showing up, slow as a glacier: no pile of invented names in a dune can stand in for them.
